name: Electrical Installation Services
tagline: Rewiring, consumer units, testing, and general electrical work for homes and businesses across Glasgow.
intro: Electrical Installation Services covers the core of what we do — the wiring, distribution, testing, and general electrical work that keeps a home or business safe, compliant, and running properly. It's the broadest of our three categories, and for good reason: whether it's a full rewire, a consumer unit upgrade, or an emergency callout at 2am, it's the same underlying skillset applied to a different job.

Everything under this category is certified to BS 7671 and, where the work is notifiable, self-certified by us as a registered NICEIC contractor — so you get the paperwork alongside the work, not as an afterthought.

faqs.q: What counts as an electrical installation service?
faqs.a: Broadly, anything involving the fixed wiring and distribution of a property — rewiring, consumer units, new circuits, testing, and general electrical repairs. It's distinct from lighting design or EV charging, which we treat as their own specialisms.

faqs.q: Do you cover both domestic and commercial installation work?
faqs.a: Yes, from a single homeowner's consumer unit upgrade through to a full commercial or industrial installation.

faqs.q: Is all of this work certified?
faqs.a: Yes, every job is tested and, where the scope requires it, certified to BS 7671 — including self-certification of notifiable work as a registered NICEIC contractor.

name: Lighting Installation & Design
tagline: Downlights, security, garden, and high-bay lighting — planned properly, not just fitted.
intro: Lighting is its own discipline, not just an extension of general wiring — layout, coverage, sensor calibration, and fitting choice all genuinely change the result. We treat it that way, planning every lighting job around the specific space before anything gets fitted.
This covers everything from a single room's downlights to full warehouse high-bay lighting upgrades — indoors, outdoors, domestic, and commercial.

faqs.q: What's the difference between lighting and general electrical installation work?
faqs.a: Lighting involves layout, coverage, and fitting-specific planning — spacing, beam angles, sensor calibration — that a general wiring job doesn't need. We plan lighting jobs with that in mind rather than treating them as a standard circuit addition.

faqs.q: Do you cover both indoor and outdoor lighting?
faqs.a: Yes, from indoor downlights and feature lighting through to garden, security, and warehouse high-bay lighting outdoors.

faqs.q: Can lighting work be combined with other electrical jobs?
faqs.a: Yes, lighting is often planned alongside a rewire, extension, or consumer unit upgrade — worth mentioning when you get a quote for other work.

name: EV & Fleet Charging Installation
tagline: Home EV chargers through to fleet and forklift charging infrastructure for commercial sites.
intro: EV charging covers a wider range than most people expect — a single home charger is a genuinely different job to load-managed charging infrastructure for a multi-vehicle fleet or a warehouse forklift fleet. We handle both ends of that range, sized properly to what's actually needed.

Supply capacity is the thing that actually determines what's possible, so every EV charging job starts with an honest look at what your existing supply can handle before we recommend a specific setup.

faqs.q: Do you install home EV chargers as well as commercial fleet charging?
faqs.a: Yes, from a single home charger through to load-managed multi-point fleet and forklift charging for commercial and industrial sites.

faqs.q: What determines whether a supply upgrade is needed?
faqs.a: Your existing supply capacity versus the number and type of charge points wanted — we assess this honestly before recommending a specific installation, including load management as an alternative to a full upgrade.

faqs.q: Can EV charging be added to an existing consumer unit or distribution board?
faqs.a: Often yes for a single home charger, provided there's capacity — larger installations may need a dedicated circuit or supply assessment, which we'll confirm before quoting.
